nodes.title: PRESENT — The Ordinary Hour
nodes.body: Ray is on shift when the incident log comes up short.

PRESENT.beat: a flashback fills in the missing hour
Ray reappears — the room has already changed
he writes the note that will send him back
the loop holds; nothing on screen contradicts it
a second Ray, older, checks the same log
the mechanism is never explained on screen

ending.title: The Loop Holds — Or Doesn't
ending.body: Whether Ray's revision actually erases the first timeline is left for the audience to decide.

legend: Yellow chips mark a beat's evidentiary status — FILM / FLASHBACK / DEDUCED (UnrealityMag device).
In dash/tape styles the same signal survives as a letter: S seen · F flashback · L seen-later · N never-shown.
The staple-rectangle box encloses how long a loop lasts, drawn to the story's own timescale (here, hours).
Ray(1) / Ray(2): the engine's own crossing-count — no hand-typed ordinal.
A dashed grey box with '?' is an ending the film deliberately leaves unresolved.
